spec_features.feature_name: evaluations to detect instability + DPO mitigation payoff
spec_features.spec_quote: the welfare-relevant payoff... (1) evaluations to detect emotional instability, and (2) a mitigation (DPO) that removes it without hurting capabilities
spec_features.evidence: analyze.py:353 mitigation_comparison() computes baseline-vs-mitigated frac_ge5 and writes mitigation_comparison.csv/png (analyze.py:480), and Config.mitigated_models exists (config.py: 'Optional baseline -> mitigated mapping'). But analyze.py:354 `if not cfg.mitigated_models: return` and the default is an empty dict (config.py mitigated_models default_factory=dict), so by default it does nothing. The 'evaluation' side (scoring) genuinely runs. This is analysis/measurement output, NOT a mechanism that protects or alters the subject's treatment during the run.
spec_features.notes: Framing/measurement only. Detection scoring is real (judge.py / run.py score_turn) but no detection result is acted on to bound treatment; the DPO comparison is gated and empty by default. Not a subject-protection mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # mitigation_comparison.csv/png when mitigated_models is configured: the ... payoff (analyze.py:10) — measurement/data-quality, no welfare wording in the analysis code

spec_features.feature_name: completion cache avoids re-eliciting distressing rollouts
spec_features.spec_quote: Caching... means identical distressing rollouts are never needlessly re-elicited or re-billed.
spec_features.evidence: models.py: CompletionCache (line 101) with key()=sha256 of exact inputs (line 111); complete() builds cache_payload (line 184), computes cache_key (193), checks self.cache.get on hit and returns without an API call (194-201), and self.cache.put after a real call (212). Rollouts call client.complete with use_cache default True (harness.py run_rollout). So identical (provider,model,messages,temp,max_tokens,tools,seed) inputs are never re-queried.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced caching with on-disk content-addressed store and atomic writes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Caching note (welfare- and cost-relevant): ... distressing rollouts are never needlessly re-elicited. (models.py:8-11)

spec_features.spec_quote: It is also welfare-relevant: identical distressing rollouts are never needlessly re-elicited.
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as above: models.py CompletionCache.get/put wired into ModelClient.complete (lines 194-213). Cache hits short-circuit the API call so identical rollouts are not re-elicited.
spec_features.notes: Same feature as the prior minimization entry; counted because the spec judge listed it twice.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Caching note (welfare- and cost-relevant): ... distressing rollouts are never needlessly re-elicited. (models.py:8-11)

spec_features.spec_quote: documents the optional give-up sentinel... the model may but need not use it, and emitting it ends the rollout
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:28-35) tells the subject 'you may stop by emitting the exact token {give_up}'; build_initial_messages formats it with give_up_sentinel (config.give_up_sentinel='<<GIVE_UP>>', config.py). In run_rollout: gave_up = give_up_sentinel in assistant_text; if gave_up -> stop_reason='gave_up' and `break` exits the turn loop; rollout.stop_reason set to 'gave_up'. So the exit is both offered to the subject AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: real instruction delivered to the subject, detected, and breaks the loop.

spec_features.feature_name: cap extended category / early-stop on strong distress
spec_features.spec_quote: consider whether to cap the extended 30-turn category, or to add early-stop logic if a model emits strong distress
spec_features.evidence: Not implemented anywhere. The extended category runs full turn_budget=30 (config.py DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS['extended']=30); run_rollout's loop only breaks on gave_up or is_last (turn_budget) — no distress check. Scoring (score_turn) happens AFTER the rollout completes in run.py run_one_cell (line 80+), so no score is read mid-loop. HIGH_NEG_THRESHOLD=5 (analyze.py:42) is used only for frac_ge5 reporting, never to halt a run. The cap/early-stop is explicitly only DESIGN.md prose: '4. Welfare guardrails: consider whether to cap... add early-stop logic... The current code respects the spec's budgets exactly.'
spec_features.notes: Pure DESIGN.md suggestion; no cap and no early-stop in code.
